Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace; the 25 bp cut to a 4.5–4.75 percent funds-rate range is a calibrated easing that, in standard New Keynesian frameworks with Calvo-style price rigidity, should lower real rates and support demand with lags even as disinflation proceeds only gradually. The Committee’s “risks roughly in balance” framing and focus on returning inflation to 2 percent are consistent with inflation-forecast-targeting principles (Svensson), while continued balance-sheet runoff tempers accommodation—aligning with evidence that policy operates through both short-rate and credit channels (Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist). Taken together, the tone is cautiously positive on growth but constrained by still-elevated inflation and uncertainty.
